subject: Capacity scenarios and network checklist for ACME private GPU pool
messages:
From: Jordan Harris <jordan.harris@acmecorp.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Cc: ops-infra@acmecorp.com
Date: 2027-03-04T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment throughput targets / initial numbers

Hi Laura,

Thanks for taking this on. We're starting the procurement and architecture review for our private Redwood deployment (VPC) and need concrete sizing guidance so we can align procurement and network changes. High-level ask: help us land on a node profile and scaling policy that meets these targets:

- Steady-state: 120 inference qps (requests/sec) for a cached Llama2-70B model, average request size ~512 tokens.
- Burst: handle up to 300 qps for short spikes (minutes) with graceful degradation.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile end-to-end under 350ms for non-streaming requests; streaming P95 target 300ms for first token.

Constraints and notes:
- We're colocating GPU nodes in our AWS GovCloud VPC and will peer with internal services over a transit VPC.
- Storage (model artefacts + KV cache warmers) will be pulled from our S3-compatible object store in the same region.
- Security team requires a shortlist of network rules and MTU recommendations (we control edge routers).

Can you share a couple of capacity scenarios (node count and type, expected per-node throughput, recommended autoscale policy, and a network checklist we can hand to our infra team)? If you can attach any spreadsheets or perf numbers that would be great.

Appreciate it — Jordan
Jordan Harris
Head of Platform Engineering, AcmeCorp
Ops: ops-infra@acmecorp.com
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Harris <jordan.harris@acmecorp.com>
Cc: ops-infra@acmecorp.com
Date: 2027-03-04T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment throughput targets / initial numbers

Jordan — thanks for the clear targets. Attached is a short playbook and three sizing scenarios (spreadsheet + network checklist) that map to the steady-state and burst objectives. Summary below; full details in attachments (acme_capacity_scenarios.xlsx, network_checklist.pdf, per_gpu_latency_estimates.csv).

High-level assumptions (call these out to your procurement/security teams):
- Model: Llama2-70B quantized (int8 perf profile in our catalog). KV cache warmed for common prefixes; average working set per replica ~30GB.
- Target payload: 512 tokens in / ~64 tokens out average.
- P95 latency target is inclusive of Redwood runtime, networking inside VPC, and object-store pulls for cold starts.

Scenario A — Balanced (recommended starting point):
- Node type: 8x A100-80GB (single node = 8 GPUs, NVLink), 2 nodes (16 GPUs total).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~140 qps (with continuous batching and KV cache), with P95 latency ~260–320ms depending on request mix.
- Burst capacity: Scale to 4 nodes (32 GPUs) to handle ~320 qps with modest queueing; autoscale trigger = sustained 95th-percentile GPU util > 60% for 120s.
- Headroom: we size ~20–25% headroom for model variants and quantization scoring.

Scenario B — Latency-optimized (lower tail latency, higher cost):
- Node type: 8x H100 or A100 with tuned kernels; 3 nodes baseline (24 GPUs).
- Expected steady-state throughput: ~200 qps with P95 ~200–260ms.
- Burst: up to 5 nodes (40 GPUs) for 500+ qps.
- Use preference routing to keep low-latency traffic on dedicated pool.

Scenario C — Cost-optimized (higher batching):
- Node type: 4x A100-80GB per node, more aggressive batching and longer queue windows.
- Expected steady-state throughput: 120 qps with P95 ~350ms (meets your stated SLO but margin small).
- Autoscale: larger step-ups to reduce idle GPU time.

Network checklist (high level):
- 100 Gbps NICs per GPU node recommended; avoid 25/40Gbps oversubscription for burst workloads.
- Enable RDMA over Converged Ethernet (RoCE v2) where available for model shard transfers and low-latency KV sync.
- MTU: set 9000 across the path to avoid fragmentation when using NVMe-over-Fabric or RDMA.
- Firewall: allow TCP/UDP 443 outbound for control plane (mTLS). Allow only internal VPC ranges for data plane; source IPs for health checks listed in network_checklist.pdf.
- QoS: shape inter-node traffic to prioritize RPC/stream frames to keep first-token latency low.

Operational recommendations:
- Warm two replicas per node for fast cold-start recovery. Eviction policy: LRU with prefetch hooks from recent traffic profiles.
- Model variants: serve quantized variant by default and keep FP16 variant as backup for quality-sensitive requests; fallback routing will add latency, include that in SLO planning.
- Monitoring & alerts: GPU util P95, inference tail latency, queue depth, network retransmits. Use the HubSpot deal link and our shared Drive doc for runbooks.

Next steps / action items:
- I attached per-GPU latency estimates used to derive the numbers — please share any deviations in your expected request mix.
- If you want, we can run a short in-region scale test (1 hour) to validate assumptions before procurement.

I'll loop Lukas and Hannah internally to confirm the per-GPU throughput numbers and the network checklist.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Solutions Architect — Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0199
Attachments: acme_capacity_scenarios.xlsx (spreadsheet), network_checklist.pdf (PDF), per_gpu_latency_estimates.csv (CSV)
From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-04T12:10:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Capacity scenarios and network checklist for ACME private GPU pool

Lukas / Hannah — forwarding Jordan's ask and my initial sizing. Two quick asks: 1) Can you confirm the per-GPU steady-state qps numbers for Llama2-70B int8 (512-token avg) we used in the sheet? 2) Any caveats on RoCE across their transit VPC / GovCloud setup we should flag to their network team?

Summary of our conservative perf numbers (from per_gpu_latency_estimates.csv):
- A100-80GB (NVLink) per-GPU sustained qps: ~8.5 qps (512-token average) when using continuous batching and cache.
- H100 tuned per-GPU qps: ~12–14 qps for same profile.
- Model warm cache multiplier: ~1.8x throughput improvement vs cold (warm KV).

Notes: the spreadsheet assumes 80% GPU util target to leave thermal/variance headroom. If we want deeper headroom (30%) we should reflect that in node counts.

Hannah — for RoCE over their transit VPC, I recall there are extra firewall and MTU constraints in GovCloud — can you add the minimal packet/port suggestions and whether we should recommend deploying a dedicated private link (Direct Connect equivalent) to avoid burst packet loss?

I'll hold sending the revised plan until we have your confirmations; want to be careful before we propose procurement counts.

Thanks — Laura
From: lukas_meyer@redwood.ai; hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
To: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-04T15:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Capacity scenarios and network checklist for ACME private GPU pool

Laura — quick notes from perf and networking:

Lukas (perf):
- Per-GPU numbers look reasonable for int8 runtime with our current kernels: 8.2–9.0 qps on A100-80GB with continuous batching (512 tokens). We benchmarked across a range of sequence lengths; 512 tokens is near our mid-range so it's consistent.
- For safety, call it 8 qps sustained per GPU for procurement (so 16 GPUs -> ~128 qps steady), and assume a 1.9x warm cache factor for expected burst headroom.
- Cold start behavior: first request after model load may add 600–900ms for file pulls unless you pre-warm with a tiny traffic spike.

Hannah (network):
- GovCloud notes: RoCE can be used inside their private rack/VPC if their cloud provider exposes SR-IOV and allows setting MTU 9000. If they transit through managed appliances that don't support jumbo frames, we need to recommend a dedicated private link (Direct Connect) or an overlay that preserves MTU.
- Firewall: they should permit UDP 4789 (VXLAN) or the tunneling ports used for their fabrics and ensure ECMP is stable across links.
- Recommend 100Gbps NICs and test with a 15-minute synthetic traffic window that ramps to 80% of link capacity to surface tail loss.

Action: we can send a short validation script and a perf harness for Acme to run (15–30 minutes) to validate node sizing. Once they signal acceptance we can schedule a 1-hour in-region run to finalize numbers for procurement.

— Luk & Hannah

On that note, Laura — you're clear to send the revised plan to Jordan with the conservative per-GPU numbers (8 qps) and the network caveats.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.ai
To: Jordan Harris <jordan.harris@acmecorp.com>
Cc: ops-infra@acmecorp.com, lukas_meyer@redwood.ai, hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-03-04T16:20:00-07:00
Subject: Final: ACME recommended capacity profile + next steps

Jordan — looping back with the slightly conservative numbers (per internal perf/network check). TL;DR: we recommend starting with Scenario A but procure for one step higher to avoid procurement delays. Full attachments and a short validation plan are included.

Final recommended procurement baseline:
- Starting deployment: 2 nodes x 8x A100-80GB (16 GPUs) — expected sustainable ~128 qps (uses conservative 8 qps per GPU).
- Procurement recommendation: order capacity for 3 nodes (24 GPUs) so you can enable a rapid scale-up to 240 qps without needing immediate new hardware if the short-term burst needs arrive.
- Autoscale: start with policy: scale out by one node when sustained GPU util >60% for 120s; scale in after util <30% for 300s.

Network & ops checklist (summary):
- 100Gbps NICs, MTU 9000 end-to-end, RoCE internally if SR-IOV supported; otherwise use dedicated private link.
- Pre-warm two replicas per node; plan for ~600–900ms cold-start penalty for model pulls unless pre-warmed.
- Run the provided 30-minute synthetic validation (we will send the harness) to verify your real-world qps and tail latency.

Attachments: acme_capacity_scenarios.xlsx, network_checklist.pdf, per_gpu_latency_estimates.csv
Links: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1aBcD_acme-private-sizing

If you'd like, we can schedule the 30-minute run next week and shadow the test. Once validated, we'll issue a final procurement note that matches the validated numbers.

Thanks — Laura
